newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait invites envoys to check Jordanians in jail.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait invites envoys to check Jordanians in jail.

text.p: Kuwait has invited foreign ambassadors in the Gulf Arab state to visit its Central Prison on Monday to check reports that Jordanian inmates were beaten last month.
The Foreign Ministry said in a statement that Kuwait took the initiative "so they (the envoys) can directly see the humane treatment Jordanian prisoners receive".

In Amman, relatives of prisoners in Kuwait say security men beat inmates in Sleibiya prison 10 days ago. One relative, who asked not to be identified, said on Thursday three prisoners were still in hospital one week after the alleged beatings.
Kuwait had earlier described the reports as lies "aimed at defaming the state of Kuwait".

The Foreign Ministry statement, carried by the Kuwait News Agency (KUNA), did not say if visits would be arranged to other prisons or name the ambassadors invited to the Central Prison on Monday. It said they represent "brotherly and friendly states".
Jordan television said on Sunday representatives from the United States, Britain and the Gulf Arab states of Qatar and Oman would visit Kuwaiti prisons on Monday.
Scores of Jordanians and Palestinians were jailed on charges of collaboration with Iraqi forces during the seven-month occupation of Kuwait in 1990-91.

Kuwait's ties with Jordan were strained over Amman's sympathy for Iraq during the Gulf crisis. Jordan has no embassy in Kuwait. Kuwait says the time has not come yet to improve ties despite Jordan's move in mid-1995 to distance itself from Iraqi President Saddam Hussein.
